messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa@minsk-retail.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 latency increase on streaming endpoint

Hi Naomi —

We started seeing sustained p95 jumps on our streaming endpoint around 08:45 PDT. Customers report slow typing UX; some sessions stalled and eventually timed out. Attached is a short timeline + a handful of sample requests. Can you confirm whether this is on our side or something on Redwood's routing/runtime?

Key notes:
- Affects model: rwd-gen-v2 (streaming)
- Impact: intermittent stalls, p95 ~ 3.8s -> 9s for a subset of requests
- Started: ~08:45 PDT, sustaining ~20–30 minutes, then intermittent

We need an ETA for mitigation and recommended mitigations on our end if any (client backoff, reduce max_tokens, switch to sync endpoint).

Thanks —
Lisa
Head of Platform, Minsk Retail

Attachments: timeline-screenshot.png, sample-requests.jsonl

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency increase on streaming endpoint

Folks — forwarding customer report. Quick triage notes below; we should align on immediate mitigations + an ask list for Product/Platform (short runway exceptions + roadmap questions).

What we know so far:
- Affected route: /v1/chat/stream (rwd-gen-v2) only when messages have long context + streaming enabled.
- Error pattern: long stalls before first chunk; once chunking starts, token rate appears normal.
- Early SRE observation (soojin): tail latency correlates with KV-cache misses on warmup windows; also saw a short spike in async batch building time.

Immediate asks (short-term):
1) Can we temporarily route Minsk to quantized model variant (rwd-gen-v2-q4) for reduced kernel latency? Marissa, can you authorize as an exception for their Dedicated pool?
2) Request SRE to push aggressive cache warm-writes for their tenant prefix for the next 2 hours.
3) Recommend Minsk drop streaming to non-streaming sync for high-latency sessions (we'll provide a client-side flag and note).

Product/Platform questions (roadmap/medium-term):
- Is per-route pre-warm / dedicated KV reservations on the roadmap? If yes, what is ETA and can we offer early access?
- Can we expose a short TTL-controlled prefix pinning for keys to avoid cold-starts on heavy fanout workloads?

I propose a short readout to the customer in 60 minutes acknowledging investigation and the three mitigation options. Soojin/karthik/ben — can you confirm who owns each bullet?

— Naomi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency increase on streaming endpoint

Quick update from SRE triage:
- Confirming correlation between elevated p95 and cache miss storms for tenant prefix minsk-retail. Warm cache hit-rate dropped from ~94% -> ~62% during the peak window.
- Observed a transient spike in scheduler queue latency (microseconds->ms) when batch windows briefly expanded; likely caused by a combination of larger-than-expected input lengths and an infrequent slow kernel path on node pool b2.

Short-term actions I can run now:
- Push a targeted KV warmup for minsk-retail across their active shards (10–15 min job).
- Force-minimize batch window for their tenant for 30 minutes (reduced batching to prioritize latency).
- Toggle route to fallback quantized variant (needs product auth for Dedicated).

I will run the warmup + batch window minimize now; requesting product signoff to perform quantized fallback for the next 2 hours. I will attach perf-heaptrace.txt after I finish the collection.

— Soojin
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency increase on streaming endpoint

Naomi — approve quantized fallback for Minsk for 2 hours. Rationale: lower kernel variance, minimal degradation to output quality for their workloads (we've got evals). Marissa signing off for Product.

Operational plan (we'll execute in parallel):
- 10:05: apply tenant route override to rwd-gen-v2-q4 for minsk-retail (will monitor errors + quality).
- 10:10: SRE to start KV warmup job and reduce batch window.
- 10:20: Naomi to send customer update acknowledging actions and ETA for next status.

Longer asks (for roadmap):
- Per-tenant pre-warm (early access) — Product wants a spec: min TTL, opt-in API, cost tradeoffs. Karthik, please draft details and impact on Dedicated billing model.
- Observability: add tenant-level warm/cold cache metrics to the Console (traceable in 2–3 sprints).

I will monitor the rollout and loop back in 30 minutes.

— Marissa
Sr. PM, Serving Platform

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: Lisa Park <lisa@minsk-retail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 latency increase on streaming endpoint

Hi Lisa — quick update and next steps (TL;DR below). We're actively investigating; we have executed a set of mitigations to reduce latency while we continue a deeper root-cause analysis.

What we did (10:05–10:15 PDT):
- Temporarily routed yours to rwd-gen-v2-q4 (quantized) to reduce kernel tail variance.
- Pushed an aggressive KV cache warmup across your active shards.
- Temporarily reduced batching on your tenant to prioritize latency.

What to expect:
- You should see p95 drop back toward normal within ~10–20 minutes as the cache warms.
- We recommend not to switch client behavior yet; if you continue to see stalls switch to non-streaming endpoint for the most latency-sensitive sessions (we can provide a QuickStart flag).

Roadmap asks (why this happened and what we will propose):
- We want to offer "tenant pre-warm" (opt-in) and per-route pinning to avoid cold-starts for production fanout patterns. Would you be open to pilot this? It will be a short-term add-on for Dedicated/Private customers.

We will follow up with a 1-hour post-mitigation summary and share logs. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority.

— Naomi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
